paragraphs.en: King Juan Carlos of Spain once insisted “kings don’t abdicate, they die in their sleep.” But embarrassing scandals and the popularity of the republican left in the recent Euro-elections have forced him to eat his words and stand down. So, does the Spanish crisis suggest that monarchy is seeing its last days? Does that mean the writing is on the wall for all European royals, with their magnificent uniforms and majestic lifestyles?
paragraphs.zh: 西班牙国王胡安·卡洛斯曾坚称：“国王不会退位，只会在睡梦中死去。”然而，令人难堪的丑闻，加上主张共和制的左翼政党在最近欧洲议会选举中受到欢迎，迫使他收回前言，宣布退位。那么，西班牙的这场危机是否意味着君主制已日薄西山？是否意味着，身着华美制服、过着尊贵生活的欧洲王室都已显露衰亡的征兆？

paragraphs.en: The Spanish case provides arguments both for and against monarchy. When public opinion is particularly polarised, as it was following the end of the Franco regime, monarchs can rise above “mere” politics and “embody” a spirit of national unity.
paragraphs.zh: 西班牙的事例既为支持君主制提供了理由，也为反对君主制提供了依据。当公众意见严重分化时，例如佛朗哥政权结束之后，君主可以超越“纯粹的”政治，成为国家团结精神的“化身”。

paragraphs.en: It is this apparent transcendence of politics that explains monarchs’ continuing popularity as heads of state. And so, the Middle East excepted, Europe is the most monarch-infested region in the world, with 10 kingdoms (not counting Vatican city and Andorra). But unlike their absolutist counterparts in the Gulf and Asia, most royal families have survived because they allow voters to avoid the difficult search for a non-controversial but respected public figure.
paragraphs.zh: 正是这种表面上超越政治的地位，解释了君主作为国家元首为何持续受到欢迎。因此，除中东外，欧洲是世界上君主最为密集的地区，共有十个王国（不包括梵蒂冈城和安道尔）。但与海湾地区和亚洲那些实行专制统治的君主不同，大多数欧洲王室之所以能够延续下来，是因为它们让选民免去了寻找一位既无争议又受人尊敬的公众人物的难题。

paragraphs.en: Even so, kings and queens undoubtedly have a downside. Symbolic of national unity as they claim to be, their very history – and sometimes the way they behave today – embodies outdated and indefensible privileges and inequalities. At a time when Thomas Piketty and other economists are warning of rising inequality and the increasing power of inherited wealth, it is bizarre that wealthy aristocratic families should still be the symbolic heart of modern democratic states.
paragraphs.zh: 即便如此，国王和女王无疑也有其弊端。尽管他们自称象征着国家团结，但其历史本身——有时也包括他们当今的行事方式——却体现着过时且无法辩护的特权和不平等。在托马斯·皮凯蒂等经济学家纷纷警告不平等加剧、继承财富的影响力不断增强之际，富有的贵族家族竟然仍是现代民主国家的象征性核心，实在令人费解。

paragraphs.en: The most successful monarchies strive to abandon or hide their old aristocratic ways. Princes and princesses have day-jobs and ride bicycles, not horses (or helicopters). Even so, these are wealthy families who party with the international 1%, and media intrusiveness makes it increasingly difficult to maintain the right image.
paragraphs.zh: 最成功的君主制国家努力摒弃或掩饰其昔日的贵族做派。王子和公主从事日常工作，骑自行车，而不骑马（也不乘直升机）。即便如此，他们依旧是与全球最富有的百分之一人群一起聚会的富裕家族，而媒体无孔不入的报道，使他们越来越难以维持恰当的形象。

paragraphs.en: While Europe’s monarchies will no doubt be smart enough to survive for some time to come, it is the British royals who have most to fear from the Spanish example.
paragraphs.zh: 欧洲各国王室无疑会足够明智，在未来一段时间内继续生存下去，但西班牙的先例最令英国王室感到担忧。

paragraphs.en: It is only the Queen who has preserved the monarchy’s reputation with her rather ordinary (if well-heeled) granny style. The danger will come with Charles, who has both an expensive taste of lifestyle and a pretty hierarchical view of the world. He has failed to understand that monarchies have largely survived because they provide a service –as non-controversial and non-political heads of state. Charles ought to know that as English history shows, it is kings, not republicans, who are the monarchy’s worst enemies.
paragraphs.zh: 只有女王凭借她那颇为平凡的老奶奶风范（尽管她十分富有），维持住了君主制的声誉。危险将随着查尔斯的到来而出现：他既追求奢华的生活方式，又持有等级观念浓厚的世界观。他未能理解，君主制之所以大体上得以延续，是因为君主提供了一种服务——担任不具争议、不涉政治的国家元首。查尔斯应该知道，正如英国历史所表明的那样，君主制最大的敌人是国王，而不是共和主义者。
